summary: Retry-scope enforcement mismatch between edge proxy and client SDK causing stale confirmation tokens and duplicate tool side-effects
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated double-execution of external tool/webhook calls for long-running streaming sessions after a recent SDK upgrade and concurrent use of BrightHealth's internal HTTP reverse-proxy. Impact: Duplicate side-effects (duplicate payment request webhook deliveries) leading to customer operational burden and potential billing issues. Environment: Production, us-east, traffic routed through company-managed reverse-proxy + our edge-proxy. SDKs involved: python client v1.9.0 (recently upgraded from v1.7.3) and a lightweight Go orchestrator.

Observed behavior: When streaming sessions experience transient network hiccups, client-side retry logic emits a retry that the edge-proxy rewrites (normalizes) certain headers and shortens the confirmation token. The SDK then sends a follow-up which the server accepts as a new request instead of a resumed session, triggering re-execution of previously-confirmed tool calls.

Fields of note: confirmation token format is the SDK-generated 128-bit nonce base64 URL-safe string in header X-RW-Confirm; edge-proxy has header sanitizer configured to trim >100 chars; reverse-proxy also applies header folding.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use python SDK v1.9.0 to open a streaming chat session that makes two sequential function/tool calls (webhook POST to customer endpoint). 2) Introduce a transient drop (iptables reject or simulate 100ms connection reset). 3) Client retries per SDK backoff and resends resumed stream metadata. 4) The company reverse-proxy rewrites/folds long headers; edge-proxy also canonicalizes header names. 5) Server treats the resumed stream as a new session because confirmation token no longer exactly matches stored in-flight key, replaying tool calls.

Expected behavior: Resumed stream should match in-flight session by preserved confirmation token or server tolerance to canonicalized token representation and not re-execute already-acked tool calls.
logs:
Customer-provided excerpt (redacted):
- client: INFO Retry attempt 1 for session s=abc123 nonce=QmFzZTY0... (128 chars)
- reverse-proxy: DEBUG folded header X-RW-Confirm into two segments
- edge-proxy: WARN header-length > 100, truncating trailing bytes
- server: INFO no matching in-flight session for token QmFzZTY0... (truncated), starting new session and re-scheduling webhooks
- webhook endpoint: 2026-03-09T21:12:32 - Received POST /payments/create (duplicate)
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Rodriguez: Customer opened ticket after finding 3 duplicates within a 24h window. They are able to reproduce reliably in prod behind their proxy.

2026-03-11 - Ethan Li: Assigned. Reproduced in staging with a synthetic proxy that truncates header > 100 bytes. Hypothesis: header sanitizer at customer-side + our edge-proxy header length guard cause token mismatch on resume path.

2026-03-12 - SRE Team: Ran a capture in us-east and confirmed a pattern where resumed session headers differ in canonicalization (case + folding) and truncated bytes. Correlation id rw-req-5591 shows two executions for same original sequence id.
2026-03-13 - Customer (BrightHealth AI): Confirmed they can disable header folding and saw no duplicates over 6h of testing. Need a longer-term fix; disabling folding is not viable for their infra.

2026-03-13 - Ethan Li: Proposed server-side tolerant matching fallback: normalize and compare first-N-bytes of confirmation token plus timestamp window; also proposed adding per-action idempotency token header as short hashed token as a workaround.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings: 1) The SDK produces a 128-char base64 nonce in X-RW-Confirm. 2) Customer reverse-proxy folds and sometimes inserts linear whitespace which changes byte representation. 3) Our edge-proxy currently enforces a hard header-length drop for safety; truncated tokens no longer match in-flight session keys. 4) When match fails, runtime treats message as new request and replays queued tool calls (webhook delivery).

Hypotheses tested: - Increasing server match tolerance to ignore whitespace and case-normalize headers prevented most duplicates in staging. - Short-hash idempotency header (sha1 of confirmation nonce) prevents re-exec when full token mangled because short-hash survives folding; however this relies on consistent hashing on client side. - Adjusting edge-proxy to preserve header bytes above 100 chars introduced DOS risk for malformed clients; needs safer boundary checks.

Tech notes: Relevant code paths: serving-runtime session resume uses exact-match on confirmation_token string (source: runtime/session_manager.go: Kill switch on mismatch). SDK change in v1.9.0 moved to longer nonce to avoid collisions; unintended side-effect with middleboxes.
resolution:
Workarounds rolled out: 1) Short-term: Customer disabled header folding on their reverse-proxy (validated no duplicates). 2) Deploy server change: tolerant resume matcher that normalizes linear whitespace, lowercases header name, and allows first-96-bytes prefix match for confirmation tokens for 72-hour grace period (rollback safe). 3) SDK mitigation: patch released in python SDK v1.9.1 to emit an additional header X-RW-Confirm-Hash (sha256 hex truncated to 16 chars) derived from nonce; server now checks this short hash as a second-level match. 4) Edge-proxy configuration: increase header-length allowance for X-RW-Confirm specifically, with a max cap and validation.

Follow-ups: - Create guidance doc for customers about header canonicalization pitfalls and recommended minimum header length handling. - Add e2e test in CI to simulate header folding/truncation and ensure duplicate prevention. - Engineering task to remove temporary 96-byte prefix matcher and rely on hash check within 30 days after SDK adoption reaches >90% of affected customers.

Status: Mitigations applied in prod us-east on 2026-03-13. Monitoring set up to alert on duplicate webhook deliveries (threshold 3 duplicates per hour).
